 Profile: Jack Lowden 
 Profile: Jack Lowden
 26th October 2026
 MI6 delves into the career of James Bond finalist Jack Lowden
   By MI6 Staff
 Share The Story 
 Jack Lowden
 An Olivier winner at 23 and six series in as MI5's least glamorous agent, Jack Lowden went into the Bray screen tests as MI6 readers' clear favourite – and a would-be first Scottish 007 since Connery. 
 From Slough House with Love 
 Jack Lowden was born on 2nd June 1990 in Chelmsford, Essex, to Scottish parents, Gordon and Jacquie, who had travelled south for IVF treatment – he and his younger brother Calum are both IVF babies, he explained to the Evening Standard in 2019. Home was the Borders village of Oxton. Since then he has collected an Olivier, two BAFTA Scotland awards for Best Film Actor, and Emmy and Golden Globe nominations for Apple TV+'s Slow Horses , with Dunkirk , Mary Queen of Scots and Benediction on the screen CV.
 Like Callum Turner, he wanted to be a footballer: "It absolutely broke my heart when I realised I wasn't going to be one," he told the Evening Standard. Instead he followed Calum – now a principal dancer with the Royal Swedish Ballet – to ballet classes, where, he told Vogue in 2022, he was quickly encouraged to try words instead. He ended up narrating his brother's ballet shows, and at about 10 or 11 he realised he could make the watching parents laugh. A shy boy, he would fill a whisky glass with ice and Diet Coke, pretend it was Scotch and sit listening to Frank Sinatra, he confessed to The Guardian; he now says Sinatra's way of bending a rhythm is what he loves about acting. His parents enrolled him in the Scottish Youth Theatre at ten, and summers in his teens brought courses at RADA.
 The stage made him. Before graduating from the Royal Scottish Academy of Music and Drama in 2011, he was already Cammy, the lead in the National Theatre of Scotland's 'Black Watch' revival, touring to London, Belfast and five American cities; The Washington Post's Peter Marks called him "quietly charismatic". In 2012 he played Eric Liddell in the West End's 'Chariots of Fire', and in 2014, aged 23, his Oswald in Richard Eyre's 'Ghosts' won both the Olivier for Best Actor in a Supporting Role and the Ian Charleson Award. Official London Theatre caught him that autumn in rehearsals for 'Electra' at the Old Vic, fake blood on his fingertips, opposite Kristin Scott Thomas. Days before the Oliviers, he recalled, fellow nominee Mark Gatiss had walked into the Wolf Hall make-up truck and hugged him. "I grew up on comedies; I don't take myself seriously in the slightest," he added, puzzled to have landed so many dark plays.
 The camera took longer. He hated it for years, he told The List in 2024, and now blames the missing audience after a childhood on stage. The BBC's War & Peace (2016), as Nikolai Rostov, brought the breakthrough, followed by Tommy's Honour , Tony Benn in A United Kingdom and Denial . In 2017 Christopher Nolan cast him as Collins, the RAF fighter pilot in Dunkirk , and he played the young Morrissey in England Is Mine , winning the part, Interview reported, with a tape recorded in character. Then came Lord Darnley in Mary Queen of Scots opposite Saoirse Ronan, and a crisis of confidence he described to The Times in 2025: "There was me at 27 thinking about stopping." Watching Ronan carry the film changed his mind.
 What followed was a run of flawed men, by preference. "I'm not a finished product and I struggle playing them," he told The Scotsman in 2020, after Calibre won him his first BAFTA Scotland award. In the same interview he named Steve McQueen, who directed him in Small Axe: Mangrove , as the best director he had worked with, and admitted he had volunteered a Boston accent for his FBI agent in Capone and instantly regretted the work. He set up a production company, Reiver Pictures, in 2019 to trap himself into making ideas happen; on its first film, Kindred , he fetched cappuccinos and forgot when it was his turn on camera. Terence Davies's Benediction , with Lowden as Siegfried Sassoon, brought a second BAFTA Scotland award in 2022.
 Slow Horses arrived in April 2022, with Lowden as River Cartwright, the disgraced MI5 high-flier exiled to Slough House under Gary Oldman's Jackson Lamb. He took it for the sarcastic, undercutting writing rather than the spying, he told Hunger in 2025, and the ex-spies he met complained about cubicles and assignments that were not sexy enough; the show, he told The Sunday Times, ends up making MI5 look grubby and boring. Alongside it came Kenneth Noye in the BBC's The Gold , a producer's credit on Ronan's The Outrun – the most useful he has felt in his work, he says, and the reason he now wants to direct – and a return to the stage in David Ireland's 'The Fifth Step', at the Edinburgh International Festival in 2024 and then in the West End opposite Martin Freeman. Being on camera, he told Hunger, "still feels like an away fixture". He married Ronan in Edinburgh in July 2024; their first child was born in September 2025. Next is Mr Darcy in Netflix's Pride and Prejudice – he asked to play him Scottish and was turned down.
 The Bond talk took off on 12th August 2026, when Richard Osman told listeners of 'The Rest Is Entertainment': "He is definitely being strongly considered." The Malay Mail pointed out that casting director Nina Gold, who is running the search, had also cast Slow Horses . In September Oldman told Canada's The Morning Show that a choice had been made: "So my fingers are crossed for Jack." Asked by the Associated Press, Ronan kept it domestic: "The dog needs to be walked, the dinner needs to be made." On 22nd October MI6-HQ reported that trade press had named him one of four finalists, with Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor, and two days later that he and O'Connor were testing at Bray Studios over the weekend, after 67% of MI6 readers backed him in a poll.
 If the call comes, he would be the first Scottish 007 since Sean Connery. The boy with the Diet Coke on ice may finally be handed something stronger.
